items.title: Crimes Act 1900 (NSW)
items.summary: The principal NSW statute defining most serious criminal offences, including offences against the person and property offences.
items.legal_significance: Primary source for the definition of many NSW offences and their maximum penalties.

items.title: Bail Act 2013 (NSW)
items.summary: Governs bail decisions in NSW using an unacceptable-risk test, with 'show cause' requirements for certain serious offences (added by amendment).
items.legal_significance: Central to the balance between the presumption of innocence and community safety; frequently amended, so always check the current version.

items.title: Bail Act 1978 (NSW)
items.summary: The earlier NSW bail statute. It was repealed and replaced by the Bail Act 2013 (NSW). Recorded here so that answers relying on it are flagged as outdated.
items.legal_significance: Historical only: do not rely on it for the current law of bail. Past HSC questions and older textbooks may refer to it.
items.syllabus_link: Crime: the criminal investigation process (bail and remand)

items.title: Young Offenders Act 1997 (NSW)
items.summary: Establishes a scheme of warnings, cautions and youth justice conferences as alternatives to court proceedings for young people.
items.legal_significance: Key example of diversion and restorative justice in the criminal justice system.

items.title: Crimes (Sentencing Procedure) Act 1999 (NSW)
items.summary: Sets out the purposes of sentencing and sentencing procedures in NSW, including aggravating and mitigating factors.
items.legal_significance: Primary source for sentencing purposes and factors.

items.title: Children (Criminal Proceedings) Act 1987 (NSW)
items.summary: Contains the conclusive presumption that a child under 10 cannot commit an offence, and procedures for criminal proceedings involving children.
items.legal_significance: Relevant to debates about raising the age of criminal responsibility; check for amendments.

items.title: RP v The Queen [2016] HCA 53
items.summary: High Court decision on rebutting the presumption of doli incapax: the prosecution must prove the child knew the conduct was seriously wrong, not merely naughty.

items.title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948)
items.summary: Adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1948; a foundational, non-binding statement of civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights.
items.legal_significance: Basis of the International Bill of Rights; much of its content is reflected in later binding treaties and customary law.

items.title: International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (1966)
items.summary: Binding treaty protecting civil and political rights, monitored by the UN Human Rights Committee. Australia is a party.
items.legal_significance: Part of the International Bill of Rights; Article 1 recognises self-determination.
aliases: International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights

items.title: Australian Human Rights Commission Act 1986 (Cth)
items.summary: Establishes the Australian Human Rights Commission, which investigates and conciliates complaints and promotes human rights.
items.legal_significance: Key domestic institution for promoting human rights.

items.title: Racial Discrimination Act 1975 (Cth)
items.summary: Makes racial discrimination unlawful and implements Australia's obligations under the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination.
items.legal_significance: Example of a treaty implemented through domestic legislation.

items.title: Mabo v Queensland (No 2) (1992) 175 CLR 1
items.summary: The High Court recognised native title and rejected the doctrine of terra nullius as applied to Australia.
items.legal_significance: Landmark recognition of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples' rights to land under Australian law.

items.title: Charter of Human Rights and Responsibilities Act 2006 (Vic)
items.summary: Statutory human rights charter requiring compatibility statements for new bills and rights-compatible interpretation of laws where possible.
items.legal_significance: Model of a statutory (dialogue) bill of rights; compare with Human Rights Act 2004 (ACT) and Human Rights Act 2019 (Qld).
aliases: Charter of Human Rights and Responsibilities Act
